about: The stored answer of the live self-test on the Checks page. The frame is the first photo of the prepared WISE 0855-0714 target; its stamp origin and time are those in data/targets/wise0855/manifest.json (a unit test keeps the two the same). The tolerances were written from the data, before the first run against the archive, and are not tuned to pass.

values.label: Photo width
values.why: A SPHEREx detector is a fixed array of this size and the reader's offsets depend on it, so no difference is allowed.

values.label: Photo height
values.why: The detector is square, as its width: no difference is allowed.

values.label: Time of the photo (MJD, UTC)
values.why: The header of a released file does not change. 0.000001 days is 0.09 seconds, and the header gives the time to 0.000000001 days, so a rounding of the last digits passes and a different file does not.

values.label: Stamp, first column
values.why: Where the reader puts the target on the photo, cut to a whole pixel (6.15 arcsec). The target must fall on the same pixel as in the stored answer, so no difference is allowed.

values.label: Stamp, first row
values.why: As the first column, for the row: the same pixel, so no difference is allowed.

values.label: Pixels in the stamp
values.why: The stamp is 64 by 64 pixels and is read whole.

values.label: Sky position after the round trip through the photo's coordinates
values.why: The target's position goes into the photo's coordinates and comes back, and must return to where it started. 0.1 arcsec is the limit the typed-position check uses against astropy (row d2-coords), a sixtieth of a pixel.
